en_title: Getting the Body Ready for Winter
en_excerpt: Autumn asks us to slow down: warming root vegetables, good fats and rest, to build immunity before the quiet of winter.
en_meta_description: How to prepare the body for winter: seasonal root vegetables, fermented foods, vitamin C, zinc, selenium and vitamin D, plus rest.
en_content:
The role of food, rest and rootedness in the transition of autumn.

Text: Simone Holz

Holistic Nutritional Therapist

Autumn is the season when mornings begin to turn colder, the sun says goodbye earlier and nature quietly changes its rhythm. The trees release what no longer serves them, and that same movement invites us to introspection, to turn inwards, nourish the roots and prepare body, mind and soul for the stillness of the

winter that is approaching.

Just as the earth reorganises itself, our body also enters this process of adaptation. It is common, in the first weeks of autumn, to feel the body heavier, muscles and joints more sensitive, a tiredness that arrives without warning or a deeper sleep that asks for more time to rest. All of this is natural: the

organism is detoxifying the excess of heat, sugar and stimulation from summer, the ice creams, the long days, the fast pace.

Autumn is nature’s gentle reminder that it is time to slow down, clear what has accumulated and strengthen our foundations. It is the time to “ground the roots” and let

go of what has already played its part, whether toxins, emotions or habits that no longer sustain our vitality.

During autumn, our body starts asking for more nutritious, denser and warmer food, and not without reason. It is the moment when we need to strengthen our

immune system and create energy reserves for winter.

This is the phase of nourishing and fortifying. Nature already offers us exactly what we need: food from the earth,

such as root vegetables – potato, carrot, beetroot, turnip, parsnip. Which are naturally richer in complex carbohydrates and minerals, providing stable energy and sustaining inner warmth. It is as if the earth itself were saying: “the time to put down roots has come.”

In Irish culture, this ancestral wisdom is reflected in the stews, coddle and soups typical of that season, warm and comforting dishes that combine root vegetables,

pulses and herbs, a simple and delicious way to warm the body and strengthen immunity.

Besides that, this is the moment to look with care at the nutrients that sustain our natural defences. Vitamin C, present in citrus fruits, kiwi and peppers,

helps protect the cells; zinc, found in pumpkin seeds and nuts, is essential for immune function; and selenium, present in eggs and

Brazil nuts, has a fundamental role in regulating thyroid hormones and in antioxidant protection. Vitamin D, often reduced by less

sun exposure, can be strengthened through foods such as oily fish (salmon, sardines) and eggs, or with professional guidance for supplementation. Small adjustments in the diet make a big difference in the body’s ability to face the cold with balance and vitality.

Another essential point is caring for the gut microbiota, the foundation of our immune system. Including fermented foods, such as sauerkraut, kefir, kombucha or natural yoghurt, helps keep the gut healthy and the body more resistant to infections. Good fats such as olive oil, avocado, seeds and nuts nourish the cells, support hormonal balance and favour the production of serotonin and melatonin, neurotransmitters linked to mood and sleep, which tend to fluctuate at this time of year. This dietary transition, at once simple and wise, stabilises blood sugar, calms the nervous system and prepares the body for the withdrawal of winter with strength and serenity.

Autumn is an invitation to pause, a space between doing and being, between the movement of summer and the withdrawal of winter. It is the moment to quieten the external noise a little and listen to the body, which wisely shows what it needs: more rest, more warmth, more presence. Preparing for winter is not only about strengthening

immunity, but about cultivating an inner state of balance and being held.

Every nutritious meal, every well-slept night, every conscious breath is an act of love and respect for the body that sustains you. When you allow yourself to slow down and nourish your roots now, you create fertile ground to go through the cold months with energy, clarity and serenity.

This autumn, listen to your body. Slow down, warm your soul and trust the natural process of the seasons.

By aligning yourself with the cycle of nature, you discover that winter is not the end, it is the rest necessary for the blossoming that will come.

Simone Holz

Holistic Nutritional Therapist
